purpose: Oxandrolone is used to help people regain weight that was lost due to surgery, a long illness, infection, or serious injury. It is also used to treat bone pain in people with osteoporosis and sometimes to help children with certain growth problems. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other medical reasons not listed here.
how_it_works: Oxandrolone is a man-made version of testosterone, a natural hormone your body already makes. It works by helping your body build protein and muscle tissue more effectively, which helps you gain back healthy weight and strength. Think of it as giving your body a boost so it can repair and rebuild itself more efficiently.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset. Acne or oily skin. Changes in sex drive. Trouble sleeping. In women, it may cause voice deepening, increased facial hair, or irregular periods. In men, it may cause breast tenderness or difficulty urinating.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems, including liver cancer with long-term use, so your doctor will monitor your liver regularly. It should not be used during pregnancy as it can harm an unborn baby. It can affect cholesterol levels and increase the risk of heart disease. Children and teenagers should be closely monitored because it can affect bone growth. It is a controlled substance and can be habit-forming, so never share it with others or take more than prescribed.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual dose is 2.5 mg to 20 mg per day, taken by mouth in 2 to 4 divided doses. Most treatment courses last 2 to 4 weeks, though some people may need it longer under close doctor supervision. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed and do not stop or change it without talking to them first.
